knowledge_point.title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x y - x + y=5$. The **tangent** line at $\left(-3,-1\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. The product rule gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=y+x\frac{dy}{dx}$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y - 1+\left(x + 1\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(x + 1\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(y - 1\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{y - 1}{x + 1}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-2}{-2}=-1
$$

The tangent line uses $m=-1$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-1\right)&=-1\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right) \\
y&=-1\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right)+\left(-1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=-1\left(x-\left(-3\right)\right)+\left(-1\right) \\
x-\left(-3\right)&=-\frac{-1}{-1} \\
x&=-4
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(-4,0\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $x^{2} + 2 x - 4 y=16$. The **tangent** line at $\left(2,-2\right)$ meets the $y$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
2 x + 2+\left(-4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(-4\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(2 x + 2\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{2 x + 2}{-4}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{6}{-4}=\frac{3}{2}
$$

The tangent line uses $m=\frac{3}{2}$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(-2\right)&=\frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right) \\
y&=\frac{3}{2}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right)+\left(-2\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $y$-axis, $x=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y&=\frac{3}{2}\left(0-\left(2\right)\right)+\left(-2\right) \\
y&=-5
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(0,-5\right)$.

question.:question/problem:
The curve has equation $2 x^{2} + 2 x + 2 y^{2} - 2 y=0$. The **tangent** line at $\left(-1,1\right)$ meets the $x$-axis at $P$. Find the coordinates of $P$.

Give exact values.

$P=(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Treat $y$ as a function of $x$. Differentiate implicitly and collect the derivative terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
4 x + 2+\left(4 y - 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=0 \\
\left(4 y - 2\right)\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\left(4 x + 2\right) \\
\frac{dy}{dx}&=-\frac{4 x + 2}{4 y - 2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the given point:

$$
m_{\mathrm{t}}=-\frac{-2}{2}=1
$$

The tangent line uses $m=1$.

Use the given point and this slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=1\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right) \\
y&=1\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)+\left(1\right)
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$. Substitute and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=1\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)+\left(1\right) \\
x-\left(-1\right)&=-\frac{1}{1} \\
x&=-2
\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore $P=\left(-2,0\right)$.
